body:
_Migrated from issue #925, filed 2026-07-15._

Split out of #924, where it blocked nothing but is worth tracking.

`koreader/plugins/cwasync.koplugin/tests/*.lua` exist and pass, but nothing runs them — not `tests.yml`, not any script. The plugin's logic has **zero automated coverage in CI**, and after #924 it carries the code that decides which highlights get deleted. A regression there destroys user data silently.

Running them is a few lines in the Fast Tests job:

```yaml
- name: Run KOReader plugin tests
  run: |
    sudo apt-get install -y lua5.4
    cd koreader/plugins/cwasync.koplugin/tests
    lua sync_logic_test.lua && lua device_annotations_test.lua
```

I did not add this in #924 because `lua5.4` is a new build-environment dependency, and rule 6 plus the autonomous-merge gate put that call with the operator rather than with an autopilot tick that would benefit from waiving it.

Worth deciding alongside: whether the whole-file Lua sources deserve a syntax gate too (`luac -p` on every `.lua`), which needs the same package and would have caught nothing so far — the value is the behavioural tests.

Related: #924's `tests/unit/test_cwasync_plugin_wire_contract.py` is deliberately Python precisely so CI enforces *something* about the plugin today.
title: The KOReader plugin's Lua tests never run in CI
